answer: Time is the scarce input. Each key broadcasts signed hardware evidence: fan curve, clock drift, the moment a disk wakes. An honest operator lays a terrace, one course per epoch, each course flush on the one beneath; break the rhythm and the edge shows a gap. A clone replays its parent perfectly, so its courses stack like a mirror image and the record goes into a spiral: identical, worthless. Split one host between two identities and the terrace splits into half-width steps, neither deep enough to pay. Ten thousand keys need ten thousand rhythms held for months, at a price no script can rent.
